lessons.request: Kitchen design could have been a lot better this is terrible (real04 run 20261028-005318-full, kitchen r_L-1_mutfak: the drawn stove got a freestanding white cooker lower than the worktop standing in a gap of the run like a dishwasher, no cooker hood, wall cabinets as separate boxes of odd widths with gaps that do not line up; real06 run 20261027-222248-full: 'What kind of a kitchen is this', 'Why is this closing the window': wall cabinets across a window, the hob a black freestanding box between base units)
lessons.lesson: A kitchen reads as one designed kitchen (general rule): a stove drawn in a counter run is the run's hob, set into one continuous worktop at its drawn span with a built-in oven under it (a freestanding range only away from a run); an agent pin never takes a hob or a fridge out of its run; every hob gets a cooker hood sized to it in the style's metal (a chimney hood on the wall, an under-cabinet hood under a wall cabinet, an island hood over an island); the wall cabinets are one run over the base run: one bottom and top line, one depth, real units of 300-900 mm whose joints line up with the base units, flush at the hood (the hood between them), never over any part of a window, a glazed door or a door (the build cuts them at the windows of the building as built), joined at the corners (a blind corner unit, a corner filler), never a lone box of odd width; a counter outline drawn inside a run is part of it; a fridge column never stands in front of a window or a pass-through; fronts, handles (on feet) and the worktop follow the style, the family's kitchen look where style.json names none. The model review's M13 flags what is left (a hob without a hood, an appliance off the worktop line, wall cabinets over a window, odd boxes, unexplained gaps, two lines) for Argus; a drawn kitchen outline that stops short of a wall (at most 0.9 m) with a drawn sink or appliance in the gap reaches that wall: the run gets that leg with the fixture built in, never a lone sink box beside the run (reading.outline_to_walls; real06 run 154514).
lessons.question: Does every kitchen read as one designed kitchen: the hob set into the worktop with an oven under it and a hood over it, every appliance of a run on its worktop line, the wall cabinets one run of real units in line with the base units, flush at the hood, joined at the corners and never over a window?

lessons.request: More decor pieces needed ... kettle in the kitchen, microwave in the kitchen etc (real06's kitchen: nothing on the counter)
lessons.lesson: Every kitchen's worktop is dressed modestly by rule (general rule): a countertop microwave at a run end against a wall or a corner, a coffee machine (or a toaster) at another end, a kettle by the sink, a utensil pot and a chopping board beside the hob, a fruit bowl on an island or a free stretch, at real product sizes (parametric with PBR materials until audited library models exist), at most one per 0.5 m of free worktop and five per kitchen, labelled added_by_ai with the reason; each passes the code checks: on the worktop (rested on the built top), off the hob and its 0.25 m side gap, off the sink, off tall units, never in front of a window, glazed door or pass-through it would reach (the build slides it along the worktop when the building as built puts a window there).
lessons.question: Does every kitchen worktop carry a few real small appliances and pieces of decor (a microwave, a kettle, a coffee machine or toaster, a board, a fruit bowl), none on the hob, in the sink or in front of a window?

lessons.request: still flying pillows all around (real04 run 20261028-005318-full, the upper-floor living room's two sofas: the cushions stood at the seat's front edge, some 0.3 m in front of the backrest, with a gap under them)

The back rays run at least 4 cm over the seat and a hit on the seat's own dome or front lip (a face looking up, or something rising less than 0.15 m over the seat) is never the back; the frame's 12 degrees is the least lean, the cushion leans at the styled 20 degrees, further when nothing is behind its upper part, and slides onto its back (rest.plan_decor, settle_back). One that cannot rest so is not built and reported, never left floating.
lessons.question: Does every cushion on a sofa or an armchair sit on the seat and lean on the backrest?

lessons.request: flying pillows (real04 cam_r_L0_e_yatak_odasi_1, bed f_L0_007 dressed with our duvet and pillows: the two decor cushions stood upright in front of the bed's pillows with no contact with the pillows behind or the mattress below)

Each piece rests on the real top by rays (S5), keeps clear of the others, is added_by_ai with its reason, and the brief's decor switch turns it off; kitchen appliances are the kitchen's.

lessons.request: what is this miniature table makes no sense (real04 run 20261028-005318-full, cam_r_L-1_salon_3: the drawn coffee table f_L-1_087 got the 3D Warehouse model 'Facit High Table W2400 D800 mm NamNam Barstool Low back Metal Leg', a 2.4 m high table with its barstools in one mesh whose box was read in feet so that it passed as a 0.73 m coffee table). lessons.request: This makes no sense and terrible sink / Terrible sink (real04 run 20261028-005318-full, cam_r_L0_e_banyo_1 and cam_r_L-1_banyo_1: five washbasins got the 3D Warehouse model 'Sink' from the zip's Kitchen folder, a double-bowl kitchen sink with a drainboard hung on the wall with a strap mirror above it). lessons.lesson: A washbasin is a bathroom basin: its names or its source say so (basin, washbasin, lavatory, vanity, bathroom sink, lavabo, Waschbecken, wastafel; the source's Bathroom folder; HSSD found_in bathroom); a model titled only 'sink' or naming a kitchen, a drainer or drainboard, a double bowl or a commercial sink is a kitchen sink and never a washbasin, a kitchen sink named for a bathroom is no kitchen sink, and every model whose title names another type (or whose title and vision check both name another type) is refused for its catalogue type (model_title title_type; the same checks as above).

(real04 run 20261028-005318-full, L0 top view between r_L0_yatak_odasi and r_L0_e_yatak_odasi: the drawn wardrobe f_L0_023 got the 3D Warehouse model 'WARDROBE' whose 0.64 m end shows a white two-pane glazed frame; the vision audit said is_type false and size_plausible false, the geometry put the detail on that end, the audit turned its front to the long face and kept it as fix). lessons.lesson: A model the vision audit said is not its type, or whose size it found odd, is not used until a second audit pass confirms its type (audit.status pending; decide.second_look, pass 2 asks it; two passes against it remove it); a model of a long-front type whose detailed face is an end while the audit turned its front to the long face gets a second look (pending): an end with a glazed panel or a window is no wardrobe front; the vision critics treat a window or a glazed frame on a piece of furniture as a wrong object (D2, swap_model) and no swap or pin takes a model the audit or its names refuse.

lessons.request: What kind of a bath is this / this bath needs to make sense (real06 run 20261027-222248-full: both bathtubs f_L0_010 and f_L1_009 got the 3D Warehouse model 'Bathtub', 1.52 x 0.74 x 0.37 m, 85 % non-manifold edges, the vision answer real_product false, size_plausible false, quality 2, audited keep). General rule: a furniture model rated 2 or lower or found no real product is not used, a fixture is fitted only at its real height (a bath's rim 0.45-0.65 m), and the bath built from code looks like a real product (rim, taps, a panel when it stands in a niche between walls)
lessons.lesson: A furniture model the vision audit rated 2 or lower, or found no real product, is not used (removed; decor keeps the doubt), and a fixture is fitted only at its real height without tolerance (a bath's top 0.45-0.65 m: fit.FIXTURE_HEIGHTS; the washbasin's working top: fit.WORKING_TOPS); when no model is left the bath is built from code as a real product: a ceramic shell with a flat rim, the bowl floor with a drain and an overflow, a chrome deck mixer at the end on a wall, and a panel under a rim band on every open side when its back stands on a wall (a niche: the front panel; a corner: the front and the open end; fixture_seat.bath_walls).
lessons.question: Does every bath stand at a real rim height (0.45-0.65 m) and look like a real product, with its taps and its panel where it stands between walls?

lessons.request: There could be better outside solutions to the grade slope (real04 run 20261028-005318-full: on the slope between the pool terrace and the garden, bare concrete box planters stacked like stairs, steps cutting through boxes, a tilted paved ramp running diagonally down the slope with a strip of lawn inside it, grey retaining walls)
lessons.lesson: A level difference in the garden is designed as a landscape architect builds it, on every project: where the ground can be graded (room inside the plot, clear of the house and the other platforms, a way past left, a natural slope gentler than the bank) the terrace meets the ground by a lawn bank of at most 1:3 or a planted bank of at most 1:2, no wall; a taller difference steps down in terraces whose tiers along one side share one level, each tier a planted bed, every tier end walled; steps are real flights (risers of at most 0.15 m, the step rule, a landing every 12 risers) that follow the ground to their foot, with cheek walls and a landing, and the terraces stop beside them (no steps through a planter); a path is laid level across, up to 1:20 a walk with an edging, up to 1:12 a sloped walk, steeper a stepped path of landings and short flights with stone step edges and a handrail over 0.45 m; a ramp only on an accessible route; retaining walls in the house's base stone with a coping (wenart/blender/grading.py; the model review's M15 and the architect's G2 check it)
lessons.question: Does the garden meet every level difference as a landscape architect would build it: banks of at most 1:3 / 1:2, terraces at one level per side and planted, flights of solid treads with cheek walls and a landing, paths level across and stepped where steeper than 1:12, a ramp only where accessibility asks, walls in the house's base stone with a coping?

lessons.request: Better solutions needed for the elevation difference outside (an aerial view of real04: a bare grey concrete retaining wall box next to the paved terrace and the pool, inside it a row of loose concrete bars or slabs lying across the grass like floating step treads, with grass between them)
lessons.lesson: Never a loose tread or slab over the grass and never a bare concrete box: every step of a garden flight is a solid block on the one below and on the ground, from the upper level to the lower one, its flight a hole in the lawn held by cheek walls that stand over the ground beside it, its last riser landing on a landing pad at the highest ground under it (a flight that would end under the lawn is not built: the edge meets the ground); a level difference is a planted slope (at most 1:3 lawn, 1:2 ground cover), terraced planters with a coping and planting, or such steps; every retaining, cheek and wing wall has a finish (the house's base stone) and a coping; the model review's M15 G2 / G6 and the architect's G2 find a tread that does not sit on its riser or the ground and a bare concrete or uncoped wall
lessons.question: Does every garden step sit on its riser and the ground (no loose tread in the grass), and is every retaining wall finished in stone or render with a coping (never bare concrete)?

lessons.request: I am not liking this is the only outside flooring (real06 / real04: the garden path and the entrance steps in the same large grey square slabs with mossy joints as the terraces and the drive, with steel handrails)
lessons.lesson: The outdoor floors are a designed set by use and style family, never one slab everywhere: the terrace and pool deck in stone or porcelain slabs with a tight joint (decking where the style calls for it), the steps and copings in a stone with a tread edge, the garden path in gravel, clay or brick pavers with a stone edging where it meets the lawn, the drive and parking in a stronger paver, all in one language with the house's base stone; a material the documents draw, or a paving the style or the brief names for the terrace, wins; every inferred floor is recorded with its reason (grading.floor_set; the model review's M15 G7 and the architect's G3 find a site whose every outdoor floor has one look)
lessons.question: Does each outdoor floor have the material of its use (terrace and pool deck, steps, garden path, drive), in one language with the house's base, never one slab everywhere?

lessons.request: makes no sense to have that table with the carpet outside, that's outside area (real04 run 20261028-005318-full, the roof terrace r_L1_teras: an indoor turned-leg pine dining table, two indoor dining chairs and a wool runner rug on the paving). General rule: an outdoor room (balcony, terrace, roof terrace, loggia, veranda, patio, any room open to the sky) and every outdoor space of the site takes no rug, runner or other indoor textile on its floor; its furniture is outdoor furniture: the fit takes only library models made for outside (named for outside or of an outdoor material such as teak, rattan, wicker, resin; never one named for inside, material tags alone do not count), else the parametric family in weather-proof materials (a steel frame with teak), recorded as a library gap; the model review (M16) and Argus find an indoor rug or an indoor model outside in every project
lessons.lesson: An outdoor room (balcony, terrace, roof terrace, loggia, veranda, patio, any room open to the sky) and every outdoor space of the site is dressed for outside: no rug, runner or other indoor textile on its floor (no rug slot, no solver rug, no outdoor-set rug; any laid by a later rule is taken out); its tables, chairs, benches and seats are outdoor furniture: the fit takes only library models made for outside (named for outside, or of an outdoor material such as teak, rattan, wicker or resin; never one named for inside; material tags alone do not count), else the parametric family in weather-proof materials (a steel frame with teak), recorded as a library gap; the architect (U1), the model review (M16) and Argus find an indoor rug or an indoor model outside in every project.
lessons.question: Is every outdoor room and outdoor space dressed for outside: no rug or carpet on its floor, and only furniture made for outside (no indoor table, no upholstered indoor chair)?

lessons.request: More lights from the ceiling needed (real04 run 20261028-005318-full: the 50.9 m2 living and dining room had one pendant over its 3.35 m table, the bedrooms one light, the halls none). General rule: every room gets the ceiling lights of its functional zones (a row of pendants along each dining table and kitchen island by its length, a light over each seating group, bed, desk and counter run) and enough general light for its floor by the lumen method (N = E x A / (F x UF x MF), the illuminance per room type scaled by the style's decor density), spread evenly, never over a wall cabinet, a tall cabinet or a stair, never in a door swing, mounted on the slope under a sloped ceiling with its lowest point 2.0 m over the floor; the model review (M17) and Argus flag a room with too little ceiling light
lessons.lesson: Every room gets the ceiling lights of its functional zones (a row of pendants along each dining table and kitchen island by its length, a light over each seating group, bed, desk and kitchen counter run) and enough general light for its floor by the lumen method (N = E x A / (F x UF x MF): a designer illuminance per room type scaled by the style's decor density, 1100 lm lamps), spread evenly; never over a wall cabinet, a tall cabinet, a wardrobe, a counter or a stair, never in a door swing; under a sloped ceiling a flush light is mounted on the slope with its lowest point 2.0 m over the floor; the decor stage hangs them whatever the AI chose (decor.ceiling_lights), the model review (M17) and Argus flag a room with too little ceiling light; the ceiling lights and pendants of one room are one model (fit.ROOM_MATCHED_DECOR_TYPES; real06 run 154514 hung three models in the living room).
lessons.question: Does every room have enough ceiling light for its size and its groups: pendants along the dining table, a light over the seating, the bed, the desk and the kitchen run, and an even general light?

lessons.request: There should have been better indoor stair solutions should be there I did not like this one
lessons.lesson: Every stair is one designed piece (wenart.blender.stair_rails): one continuous balustrade per open side that follows the flights and turns at newel posts round the landing or the winders at the well, the handrail 0.90 m over the nosing line (1.0 m on a level edge), no rail crossing another or stopping short, none through a tread, a wall or the floor above (beside the floor guard above, that guard takes over); a wall handrail on brackets with returns where a flight is wider than 1.0 m or would hold none; infill gaps under 0.11 m in the house's style (glass with a cap, slim bars, timber slats, turned or wrought balusters); a light structure (thin plate or slim strings) in light styles, the closed under-stair only on the floor; the winders start at the landing's level (no double step). The model review M18 checks it.
lessons.question: Do the stairs read as designed stairs: one handrail per side turning at newels, nothing crossing or stopping short (M18), a light structure where the style is light?

lessons.request: this solutions still not good enough and columns are too thick there is a gap between balcony and small roof there should not be a gap (real06 run 20261028-154514-full, ext_1: the veranda's lower roof stops about 1 m short of the balcony slab, 0.40 m posts under a light roof)
lessons.lesson: A light roof (veranda, porch) meets the slab or balcony above it: only a house roof or slab at most 4 m above its floor counts as cover (outdoor.ROOF_COVER max_m), an uncovered strip under 0.6 m is roofed too (SLIVER_M), a drawn lower roof is matched by its share of the region, and its pitched polygon is the union of the drawn outline and the roofed area. Inferred posts under a light roof are at most 0.15 m (LIGHT_POST_M); a drawn column under a slab corner reaches the slab. Every change in assumed. lessons.question: Does anything built inside the house (a door, its frame or open leaf, a wardrobe, a shelf, decor) cross the roof or the ceiling over it, so it shows from outside?

lessons.request: These things need fixing also, maybe include some better car models (30 Oct 2026, real04 run 20261029-201533-full: pairs of small stone blocks on the paved terrace by the pools; the parking has one poor car model)
lessons.lesson: A site element is built only where it makes sense, on every project: a flight up out of a sunken platform onto another surface is cut into that surface (its treads open to the sky, never buried under a drive with only its cheek walls standing as blocks: site.cut_flights); no kerb where another surface abuts the edge (kerb_gaps); a path ends where it arrives at a surface and never runs into a building (path_stop; a terrace's path may end at a drive); a labelled site area held by its drawn surface is built, not lost (Argus C5). A parking gets well-made library cars (textured, at least 15k faces, no toy texture), the front on the long side of the model's own box (site_models.car_frame; the library audit refuses a turn onto a vehicle's side), scaled uniformly into a real car's size (4.2-4.9 x at most 2.1 x 1.25-1.75 m), parked in its bay's direction along the parking's edges near its label, one model per bay. Checks: model review M15 G8, Argus C5.
lessons.question: Is every object on the paved site a real thing that makes sense where it stands (no stray stone blocks or step pieces on a level paving), and does every drawn parking hold well-made, realistic car models?

lessons.request: I did not like this bed (30 Oct 2026, real04 run 20261029-201533-full: our procedural duvet's sides ripple like melted foam, the turned-down band is a thick slab, the pillows sit crumpled at the headboard)
lessons.lesson: Every bed's bedding looks like a real made bed, for every style family (wenart.blender.bedding_parts cover_grid, textiles.drape_cover, bedding_set): the duvet's top is a smooth envelope over the mattress (it bridges a library mattress's own quilting and dips, never follows every ray hit) with a few soft wide folds (ridges about 25 cm wide, at most the family's wrinkle); over each edge it rounds on its own height, then hangs straight down one plane per side, outside the bed at every height (a wider frame cleared by a gentle flare, the bed's own rail or footboard stops it), every edge point's drop scaled to one level hem (a straight even hem), with a few soft wide folds (46 cm pitch, 1-1.8 cm) growing to the hem; the cloth thins to its seam over its last 6 cm (a rounded hem, never a cut slab); the turned-down top sheet is a thin band (a 7 mm sheet, a neat 2-4 cm fold wrapped round the duvet's head edge, down the sides with the duvet); the pillows are plump with crisp pillowcase edges (a flange: 4 cm on a euro sham, 1.5 cm on a pillow, piping on a cushion); lying pillows without a headboard stay on the bed. The look is measured on every build (bedding_parts.cover_smoothness: the top and the hanging sides within 6 mm of their own smooth surface over 30 cm, the hem within 12 mm of a level straight line); M30 and Argus U34 flag a lumpy duvet or a wavy hem. One mesh per bed from vertex arrays.
lessons.question: Does every bed's bedding look like a real made bed: a smooth duvet with gentle natural folds and a straight hem, a thin turned-down sheet band, neat plump pillows standing against the headboard?

lessons.request: Head section of this bed needs a rework (30 Oct 2026, real04 run 20261029-201533-full: two flat lying pillows low in front of a tufted headboard, a gap between mattress and headboard, no shams or standing pillows)
lessons.lesson: The head of every bed is made up: a bed's back rays take their first hit in the head zone (a raised head section or a roll nearer the middle no longer hides the headboard behind it, rest.place_leaning), the euro shams and the sleeping pillows first stand on what lies at the head against the headboard behind their upper part (a model's own flat pillows, a panel raised on posts), a gap between the mattress and the headboard (rest.bed_head: the top dropping 4 cm, the gap at least 8 cm deep) is bridged (their base on the mattress, leaned back until their upper part reaches the headboard) and closed by a fitted sheet over it (textiles.gap_sheet); a made-up library bed whose own pillows lie flat (a bump under 0.22 m over its cover) on a bed wide enough for euro shams gets our standing set on them, its duvet kept (bedding_parts.dress_mode pillows). Argus U34 and M30 flag a gap left open.
lessons.question: Is the head of every bed made up: euro shams and pillows standing against its headboard (a headboard with a gap or posts found too), with no bare gap between mattress and headboard?

lessons.request: I am guessing these orange things are towels, they need more detail, a lot more detail (30 Oct 2026, real04 run 20261029-201533-full bathroom: rolled towels as faceted cylinders, the hanging towel a flat slab)
lessons.lesson: Every towel of every bathroom reads as a real towel (wenart/blender/towel_parts.py, used by every towel of wenart/blender/bath_parts.py: the towel rail B7, the towel shelf B18, the towel bars B25, the walk-in shower's bar B16, the vanity's open shelf B3/B12 and the column's cubbies B5): cloth of a real thickness, a closed mesh with rounded edges, never a cylinder or a plate. A rolled towel shows its spiral end (2.25 turns of the folded cloth with a groove between them, the outer end lying on the roll), rounded turn edges, a little flattened on its shelf; a folded towel has one soft rounded fold at the front, its two layers and hems at the back (the upper one shorter, pillowed), and a stack is slightly uneven in place, turn and height; a towel over a bar has both layers (the front longer), a soft curve where it leaves the bar and a little belly under it, gentle vertical folds growing towards the hem, a slight sag, rounded hems and a flat-woven band near the front hem. The material is terry cloth (finishes fabric_terry: the wenart_weave loop pile as a deep bump, roughness 0.97) in the room's towel colour (B26), a pair's or a stack's second towel in its lighter shade (towel_parts.towel_shade), the band a smooth cotton weave in the same colour. Cheap: vertex lists in the host's one mesh (a roll under 700 faces, a folded towel under 600, a hanging towel with its band under 1800). Checks: tests/test_towels_20261030.py (closed meshes, the spiral, the folds and layers, the two layers over the bar, the band, the face counts, the terry material and its loop-pile bump).
lessons.question: Do the towels read as real towels: rolled with a spiral end, folded in soft stacks, hanging over the bar in two layers with a curve, folds and a hem band, in a terry-cloth material?

lessons.request: salon inspiration (30 Oct 2026, photo P16: a living-dining room: full-height handle-less wall panels with a black-lined lit niche, a very large framed line-art print over a plank wood dining table on black trapezoid legs, green velvet chairs, a fringed rug, black ceiling track spots with mini pendants over the table, black round wall discs, a TV on a plain wall over a low floating wood console with a black fluted strip, tall narrow black-lined lit shelf niches beside it, a black slat column by the passage, two sculptural boucle armchairs, a round travertine drum coffee table, a round striped rug, sheer curtains, herringbone oak)
lessons.lesson: Every living or dining room of the modern-warm families (modern, contemporary, minimal, japandi, scandinavian) takes the P16 set where the room has the walls and the floor for it (wenart.furniture.salon_details; each item added_by_ai with its reason, every floor item through the placer's checks, every wall item off doors, windows, panelled walls and the other wall items, nothing drawn moved): a low wall-backed TV unit becomes a floating wood console with a black fluted strip (its footprint, place and top kept) with a tall narrow black-lined lit niche of books and vases on each side where the wall has room, and the TV wall stays plain (a print over the TV or where a niche stands leaves it, logged); the print over a dining table is about 2/3 of the table's length (every family; at most 2.0 m and 0.8 of its free wall, up to 1.6 m high); the row of pendants over the table becomes one fixture, black mini pendants on a black ceiling track where the scheme has track lights or a slim black linear pendant where its statement is linear (the lights plan counts it as the whole row); a rug under the dining set and under every sofa group where none lies (every family, the decor rules' trust and cuts); the table's centre item becomes a centrepiece set (a glass vase of pampas grass, concrete candle holders, a low bowl) between the place settings and under the pendants; full-height handle-less panels with an inset black-lined lit niche on a free wall of the dining zone (not the TV wall, not behind the chairs, their doors' clearance free, never under a sloped ceiling); a near-square coffee table becomes a round travertine drum on a round rug with concentric stripes; two black round wall discs on a free wall (never the TV wall). Products by design in wenart.blender.salon_parts. Not built: the slat column by a passage (R46), boucle on the accent armchairs (R47: no boucle model in the library), the fringe on a library rug, the print's black frame and line art (the fit picks the art). lessons.question: Do the living-dining rooms reach the P16 reference where their family allows: handle-less full-height wall panels with a lit niche, a very large framed print, a plank table with a fringed rug, track spots with mini pendants, a TV over a low floating console with lit shelf niches beside it, sculptural armchairs, a round stone coffee table on a round rug, sheer curtains?

lessons.request: I did not like this lamp table combo (30 Oct 2026, real04 run 20261030-043021-full, living room: a tall spindly round side table on a grey four-star swivel base with a big white drum-shade lamp on an hourglass black and brass base almost as wide as the table top)
lessons.lesson: A table lamp is chosen with its host table: its shade at most 60 % of the top's smaller side (50 % on a light pedestal, never over 75 %), beside a sofa or a bed 0.75-1.15 x the table's height, never shrunk under 85 % of its real size; no novelty lamp, no task or desk lamp beside a seat while another fits; a side table, nightstand or coffee table stands on a solid base (no office, swivel or star base outside a study: fit.stable_base); the lamp records its limits (run 20261030-043021-full: a Nelson swivel end table with an oversized drum lamp).
lessons.question: Does every table lamp sit in proportion to its table (shade at most about 60 % of the top, real size, eye-level height beside a sofa or bed) on a solid side table that matches the room, never an office, swivel or star-base table, a novelty lamp or a work lamp beside a seat?

lessons.request: I like the new Teras furnitures better but a different flooring is needed which must be suitable for the outside (30 Oct 2026, real04 run 20261030-043021-full, the L1 roof terrace r_L1_teras: the new lounge set is liked; its floor is not an outdoor floor)
lessons.lesson: A roof terrace, a balcony or a loggia of the house takes the style family's terrace floor (grading.raised_floor: stone or porcelain slabs with a tight joint, or a wood deck for the families that use one; a stone the style names is kept), never the garden paving with grass in its joints, gravel or the interior floor; the room's furniture stays (run 20261030-043021-full: the roof terrace had the garden slabs with mossy joints).
lessons.question: Is the floor of every roof terrace and balcony a real outdoor floor (stone or porcelain slabs with tight joints, or a wood deck), never garden slabs with grass in the joints or an indoor floor?

lessons.lesson: A bag reads as a real product: the weekend holdall (wenart.blender.holdall) has a soft barrel body in the item's colour with a slight sag, a leather base band and piping round its end panels, a top zip with its slider, pull and garage tabs, two rolled leather handles on riveted tabs joined by a wrap, a front pocket with its zip, a shoulder strap on D-rings with steel clips, base studs; never a blob with stick handles.
lessons.question: Does every bag read clearly as a real bag (a body with seams or piping, a zip, real handles on tabs, a strap and hardware), never a plain blob with stick handles?

lessons.request: I did not like these sofas here maybe used in another project but not here (30 Oct 2026, real04 run 20261030-043021-full, the L1 play, activity and rest room: two white wooden daybeds with drawers under the seat and panelled backs face each other as the room's sofas)
lessons.lesson: A daybed (a day bed, trundle, guest bed or futon) is never the sofa, corner sofa or chaise of a living, dining, hall or balcony room (fit.daybed_room), unless the piece itself asks for a daybed in a cottage, farmhouse, scandinavian, rustic or coastal family; guest, child's and study rooms keep daybeds; an agent pin to one is refused with the reason (run 20261030-043021-full: two HEMNES daybeds as the play room's sofas).

lessons.request: these 2 sections still not solved properly, it needs to be only road, also in the project roads going to nowhere we can increase the roads outside, first the project section and closed off sections and outside roads (30 Oct 2026, real04 run 20261030-043021-full, the front drive: at both ends of the paved drive in front of the houses stone step blocks stand in the road beside the sunken strips at the facades; the drive ends at the lawn on both sides and leads to no road)
lessons.lesson: A road stays only road and leads somewhere: a flight up onto a drive or a parking is set into its sunken platform, its top step at the road's edge, the edge's railing open there, no steps or cheek blocks in the road (site.up_flight flight_inward, ROAD_KINDS); a dead end of a drive (a strip's square end with nothing paved past it) runs on in the drive's paving to the plot's edge (at most 12 m) and a 6 m asphalt street runs along that plot edge outside the plot across the ground (site.road_dead_ends, outside_roads).
lessons.question: Is every drive only road (no steps or stone blocks standing in it), and does every drive lead somewhere: on to the plot's edge and a street outside, never ending at the lawn?

lessons.request: too many pillows in this bed, also the headrest needs to be re-done I did not like the headrest (30 Oct 2026, real04 run 20261030-043021-full, a bedroom: a double bed with eight pillows and cushions stacked in three rows, an arched camelback upholstered headboard)
lessons.lesson: A bed shows at most five pillows and cushions in two rows (a double: 2 shams, 2 sleeping pillows, at most 1 lumbar; with no headboard the accent pair instead of the shams and no lumbar; a single: 1 pillow and at most 1 cushion); every standing sham or pillow rests on the mattress against its headboard (80 % of its face held within 3 cm, else it leans back to 20-40 degrees, else it lies flat), on parametric and dressed library beds alike; arched, camelback, saddle-back, wingback, sleigh and scalloped headboards rank last outside classic or romantic families, and our beds take the family's headboard (modern: channel tufting; minimal, industrial: a plain panel; scandinavian, japandi, rustic, mediterranean: wood slats; classic, transitional: piping and buttons).
lessons.question: Does every bed show at most five pillows and cushions in two rows, each resting on the mattress against its headboard (none standing over a low headboard), with a rectangular headboard in the room's family style (no arched or camelback unless classic)?

lessons.request: A laptop on this table could have even nice, also some stationary (30 Oct 2026, real04 run 20261030-043021-full, a bedroom desk: an oak desk with a drawer pedestal and an office chair, its top bare)
lessons.lesson: Every built desk carries its work set whatever its reading status, form or model: an open laptop facing its chair, stationery beside it (two notebooks and a pen pot with pens and pencils: wenart.blender.desk_parts), a desk lamp at a back corner unless a lamp, a pendant over the desk or a wall unit's LED already lights it; all on the desk's top, never on a shelf under it; a twin room's copied decor too.
lessons.question: Does every desk carry an open laptop facing its chair, stationery (notebooks, a pen pot) beside it and a desk lamp unless something already lights it, all on its top?

lessons.request: books not staying properly also we need more realistic books (30 Oct 2026, real04 run 20261030-043021-full, the living room: a stack of three block books on a glossy white coffee table with raised curved edges hangs over the raised edge, half off the flat top)
lessons.lesson: A hard decor item on a top (books, a vase, a tray) rests with its whole footprint on the level top: a 3 x 3 grid of rays out to 98 % of its sides must all hit, the hits level within 6 mm; it moves towards the host centre (8 steps) until it is, never over an edge, a raised lip or a rim (rest.place_on_top, EDGE_SPREAD, LEVEL_TOL_M); books are the detailed book models of UL154.
lessons.question: Does every object on a table or shelf sit wholly on its flat top, never hanging over an edge or perched on a raised lip, and are the books real-looking?

lessons.request: Here models needs more details (30 Oct 2026, real04 run 20261030-043021-full, a bathroom: the lit open shelf tower holds crude objects: a box with two square holes, a few pebbles on a tray, a reed diffuser of three sticks with white balls, a green egg on a white cylinder; the towel rail and the flush plate are plain)
lessons.lesson: Every object on a bathroom shelf, vanity or towel shelf is a real product (wenart.blender.bath_objects): pump bottles with a ribbed collar, a pump with its nozzle and a label band; lidded jars with cotton balls or pebbles; a reed diffuser (bottle, collar, fanned reeds); a ceramic pot with soil and leaf blades on stems; glass flacons with a collar and cap; a soap dish with a bar; a candle in a glass; a woven basket with rolled towels; never a box with holes, balls on sticks or a coloured egg.
lessons.question: Does every object on a bathroom shelf, vanity or towel shelf read as a real product (pump bottles with pump and label, lidded jars with their contents, a diffuser with fanned reeds, a leafy potted plant, flacons, a basket of towels), never a plain box, a ball on a stick or a coloured egg?

lessons.request: I like this sofa but resting pieces seems like not connected to sitting, requires fixing (30 Oct 2026, real04 run 20261030-043021-full, the living room's white low L-shaped modular sofa: the back pieces stand as separate blocks behind the seat deck, not joined to it)
lessons.lesson: A sofa's or a chair's rests (its back, back cushions, arms) touch its seat: measured on the model's points (not boxes, an L's box covers everything), a rest 5 mm-10 cm off its seat slides against it with what lies on it, a rest held over its base comes down onto it, the two backs of an L meet at the corner; the model's own back angle kept; moves recorded (soft_seats.rest_plan; review M33 / Argus U36 rest_apart; run 20261030-043021-full: the library 'Sofa en L' had its backs 4 cm behind the seat).
lessons.question: Does every sofa's and chair's back, back cushion and arm touch its seat (no gap over 5 mm, nothing floating over its base), and do the two backs at an L's corner meet with no gap?

lessons.request: These switches requires a rework (30 Oct 2026, real04 run 20261030-043021-full: the plate in the bathroom (the wall-hung WC's dual-flush plate) reads as a black picture frame with two flat white panes, much too large and flat)

lessons.question: Is the WC's flush plate a real dual-flush plate (a slim rounded plate with a small and a large button, a fine gap and a line on each, in the room's fixture finish), never a frame with two flat white panes?

lessons.request: On the top down views do not use these tags, I am not able to see what is behind (30 Oct 2026, real04 run 20261030-043021-full, the top-down views top_L-1 / top_L0 / top_L1: every room carries an opaque white label box with its name and type over the furniture)

lessons.request: These 2 lights together not making sense, keep the black one and make it give light (30 Oct 2026, real04 run 20261030-043021-full: a black linear canopy with four wire-cage pendants hangs next to a glowing white octagonal ceiling light in the same ceiling; the pendants give no light)
lessons.lesson: A pendant (a single one, a cluster, a linear pendant, a track of mini pendants) is the only light of its zone: no rig or decor flush ceiling light within 1.5 m of its footprint; the dropped fixture's light moves into the pendant as warm 2700 K point lights split over its bulbs (counted from the model or its title), its bulbs glow; a pendant that replaces nothing gives one ceiling light's 1100 lm; every drop is recorded (lighting rig 'dropped'). A light under a sloped ceiling sits on the slope: its top centre on the ceiling plane, tilted onto it, with a hang record (furniture.slope_seat; run 20261030-043021-full: a hall's black 4-light pendant beside two white flush lights, six L1 lights 4 cm under the slope).
lessons.question: Is every pendant the only light of its zone and lit (warm, glowing bulbs), with no flush ceiling light within about 1.5 m of it, and does every light under a sloped ceiling sit on the slope with nothing floating?

lessons.request: There should be better solution than these things in the house entrance points make it make sense (30 Oct 2026, real04 run 20261030-043021-full, the side of the house: flat white slabs stick out of the stone wall over the entrance doors, one of them just under the eaves, with no support, frame or light)
lessons.lesson: An entrance canopy makes sense: none where the roof's eaves pass less than 0.5 m over it or a balcony or the floor above reaches out over the door (they shelter it); under a window over the door's span it sits 0.15 m under the sill, none when that leaves no room over the door; the canopies of one wall line share one height; and it is a real product: a slim anthracite metal canopy with deeper front and side fascias (the drip edge), a wood soffit, two black steel tie rods from its front corners to wall plates above it, the wall lights beside the door (facade.canopy_height, canopy_parts; run 20261030-043021-full: flat white slabs at two heights over the side doors).
lessons.question: Does every entrance canopy make sense (a real framed canopy with its fascia, soffit and tie rods or brackets, at one height along its wall, never under the eaves or a balcony that already shelters the door), never a bare white slab stuck out of the wall?

lessons.request: fenced neighbouring plots and some roads coming to this project (30 Oct 2026, the user's answer to what 'closed off sections and outside roads' means in UL162: the neighbouring plots around the project as fenced plots, and roads that lead to the project from outside)
lessons.lesson: The project sits among its neighbours: plots of the project plot's size on its sides, 8 m apart, cut back from the roads, each fenced 0.3 m inside its edge with a 3 m gate on the edge nearest the road (site.neighbour_plots, NEIGHBOURS); a road comes to every drive end from outside, square to the street, on across the ground (outside_roads); no neighbours or roads drawn: inferred.
lessons.question: Does the project sit among fenced neighbouring plots with roads that come to it from outside, never alone on an empty lawn with its drive leading nowhere?

lessons.request: Do the 3D export only once, at the end rest stays the same (30 Oct 2026, the user on the step times of real04 run 20261030-112241-full: the 3D export ran four times, about 3.5 min each, after the phase-5 build and again after the big loop's rebuild, for the house and the open-kitchen variant)
lessons.lesson: A run exports each scene's 3D files once, at the end, of the final scene: every export the final chain asks for (phase 5, the big loop's final stages, a rebuilt variant) waits (Orchestrator.defer_export) and exports_at_end runs each once in run order after the last round, also when the chain stops early; everything else stays as it was (run 20261030-112241-full: four exports of about 3.5 min each).

lessons.request: I did not like the lamp (30 Oct 2026, real04 run 20261030-112241-full, a ground-floor bedroom: a classic antique-brass chandelier with white bell shades over the bed of a modern concrete-walled room); again on the play room's dining table: "also I did not like the lamp" (a crystal-drop chandelier over a modern dining table); and on the open kitchen: "also I did not like the white lamps" (two tiered white shell chandeliers over the peninsula, 'chandelier 01')
lessons.lesson: A library model is used only when its own title names no style the project's family may not carry (catalog.title_style_clash: 'Classic', 'Traditional', 'Antique', 'Victorian', 'crystal' ...; a finish name such as 'antique brass' does not count; a chandelier without a modern form word such as mid-century, mesh, Edison, sputnik, linear or globe is the classic form): the title is the maker's word, the styles tags only the vision judges' guess (real04: a 'Classic ... Chandelier ... Antique Brass' tagged modern and scandinavian, a '5-Light Chandelier' and crystal 'Designer chandeliers' in a modern house). Every pick of furniture and decor goes through catalog.styles_match.
lessons.question: Does every light and piece carry the house's style family, with no classic chandelier, crystal drops or antique fittings in a modern home unless the brief asks for them?

lessons.request: laptop and stationary can be more detailed models they are too plain (30 Oct 2026, real04 run 20261030-112241-full, the bedroom desk: a flat slab laptop, plain notebooks and a plain pen pot)
lessons.lesson: A desk's laptop, monitor and stationery are real products (desk_parts): a rounded aluminium laptop opened 110 deg with single keycaps, speaker grilles, a glass trackpad, a hinge, a slim bezel with a camera and a logo; every screen shows a switched-on desktop (menu bar, a document window, a picture window, a dock; screen_ui glows faintly and lights nothing); A5 notebooks with rounded covers over a page block, an elastic band and a ribbon, a leather one with a phone and a pen on it; a hollow ceramic pen pot with pens (tip, cap, clip) and sharpened six-sided pencils; every part at real size inside the item's box.
lessons.question: Do the laptop and the stationery on every desk look like real products (keys, trackpad, screen, notebooks with pages, pens with clips)?

lessons.request: I did not like this bed (30 Oct 2026, real04 run 20261030-112241-full, a ground-floor bedroom with slatted walls: a glossy black bed under a plain white duvet slab, grey and white pillows leaning)
lessons.lesson: A home's bed is a real residential product, never a care, hospital or motion bed: a model whose title names one (adjustable, hospital, nursing, care bed, medical, motorised, electric bed, massage, profiling: fit.CARE_BED_WORDS) is no candidate for a double or single bed (fit.use_misfit, rule fit.product_use, reason logged), and an agent's pin cannot bring it back. real04's f_L0_021 was the 'Komfi Adjustable Bed' (a sectioned glossy black and chrome base whose uneven top tore the throw), disliked on 28 Oct (UL73) and again on run 20261030-112241-full; its refit takes a home bed.
lessons.question: Does every bed look like a good real bed of the style family, with made bedding that is not a flat slab?

lessons.request: this wall texture seems to be used too much in the house, reduce it down (30 Oct 2026, real04 run 20261030-112241-full: the wood slat wall panelling on whole bedroom walls, in many rooms); again on the play room: "same wall texture reduce"
lessons.lesson: A feature finish is a room's accent, never the whole house: the walls slot (every room's walls) keeps a plain finish (plaster, paint, concrete) unless the brief names the finish (exterior_checks.wall_slot_problems: wood slats, panels, brick, stone, wallpaper or tiles are refused there); at most two rooms of a house (a twin counts, a variant level is its own version) get a vertical slat or fluted wall, the next rooms take the bundle's art in its place (room_schemes.SLAT_ROOMS_MAX). real04 run 20261030-112241-full: an Argus set_material walls wood_slat clad 48 wall faces of every room.
lessons.question: Is a feature finish (slats, panels, wallpaper) used on one accent wall of a few rooms only, never on every wall of the house?

lessons.request: Table seems to be going through the chairs (30 Oct 2026, real04 run 20261030-112241-full, the top-floor play room's dining set: a turned-leg table with a drawer apron, two grey shell chairs whose seats and backs pass through the table top and legs)
lessons.lesson: A chair never stands through its table: a round drawn table is built round (a round library model, its title says round, else our round pedestal table; a square model is refused, also for the agent's swap); a chair tucked under a table with corner legs keeps out of a 0.10 m square at each corner, the build pulls it to a leg-free place (a drawn chair moves at most 0.5 m in all, adjusted_by_ai), else it keeps its place and is reported (a build warning, the architect's F5, the score's F9 'stands in the corner legs'). real04 run 20261030-112241-full: a square turned-leg table on a drawn round cafe table, its legs in both chairs.
lessons.question: Does every chair stand clear of its table's top, apron and legs?

lessons.request: Door style is good but it is too plain, make it better (30 Oct 2026, real04 run 20261030-112241-full, a glazed outside door seen from inside: a flat oak frame and stile with one big pane, a plain casing, a black lever)
lessons.lesson: Every parametric door of a style family is joinery of its family, not boxes: glazing beads round the glass on both faces, a profiled architrave (a stepped casing with a raised fillet in the light families, a ramped casing with a rounded back edge on plinth blocks in the period families), hinge knuckles with tips, the lever on a round rose or a backplate with a neck, a lock cylinder, and on an outside door a weather bar at the foot of its outside face; library doors' frames take the same architrave. The style the user likes stays; only the detail is added.
